claims.text: The untreated refractory high-entropy alloy has high strength.
The untreated alloy exhibits an energetic impact response.
The untreated alloy has limited ductility and localized deformation.
Coarse grains and brittle intergranular features cause the alloy's localized deformation.
The proposed intervention is addition of approximately 0.5–1 at.% carbon followed by tailored thermomechanical processing.
Controlled carbon doping and thermomechanical processing will produce uniformly distributed nanoscale carbide precipitates along grain boundaries.
The carbide precipitates will refine and stabilize the microstructure.
Carbide precipitates will stabilize grain boundaries.
Carbide precipitates will impede catastrophic shear-band formation.
Carbide precipitation will promote uniform plastic flow by enhancing grain-boundary sliding.
Carbide precipitation will promote uniform plastic flow through improved dislocation accommodation.
The precipitate-containing alloy will retain the high strength of the refractory matrix.
Carbon doping and carbide precipitation will preserve impact-induced energy release.
The treated alloy will achieve approximately a 15–25% increase in tensile elongation relative to the untreated baseline.
The treated alloy will deform more uniformly under load than the untreated baseline.
The treatment will not reduce yield strength by more than 5% relative to the untreated baseline.
The treatment will not reduce impact-induced energy release by more than 5% relative to the untreated baseline.
The improvement requires carbon content to remain within a narrow concentration window.
Excess carbon or imprecise heat treatment may embrittle the alloy or otherwise deteriorate its mechanical properties.
Known effects of interstitial doping and precipitate strengthening make the proposed approach plausible.
